task: Build the list of Fibonacci numbers up to 13, that is 1 1 2 3 5 8 13, by writing and evaluating lisp code; store the list as answer. When achieved, evaluate (final true).
lesson: Today I learned that even tiny Lisp programs can solve complex math tasks with just a few lines of code.

nodes.code: (begin (define (fib n) (if (<= n 1) n (+ (fib (- n 1)) (fib (- n 2))))) (let ((lst (list 1 1))) (while (<= (nth lst 1) 13) (set! lst (cons (fib (len lst)) lst))) (set! out (reverse lst)) (rlm-set answer out) (final true))
